references.text: Isaiah prophesies about the anointed one upon whom the Lord's Spirit rests, because the Lord has anointed him – a messianic text that Jesus himself applies to himself. This points to the fact that the One God sends speaks God's words and has received the Spirit without measure ([ref:Jes 61:1|Isaiah 61:1]).

Moses promises that God will raise up a prophet like him, and God will put His words in his mouth, and he shall speak all that God commands him. This is the background for why the One God sends speaks God's words ([ref:5 Mos 18:18|Deuteronomy 18:18]).
Jesus says that His teaching is not His own, but belongs to Him who sent Him. This confirms that the One God has sent speaks God's words ([ref:Joh 7:16|John 7:16]).

Jesus says that He speaks to the world what He has heard from the Father, and that He does nothing on His own but speaks as the Father taught Him. This expands on the idea that the One sent by God speaks God's words ([ref:Joh 8:26-28|John 8:26-28]).

Jesus declares that He has not spoken on His own, but that the Father who sent Him has given Him a command about what He should say. This confirms that He speaks God's words ([ref:Joh 12:49|John 12:49]).

From Christ's fullness we have all received, grace upon grace. The idea of Christ's fullness points to the fact that He has received the Spirit without measure, and that His riches overflow to believers ([ref:Joh 1:16|John 1:16]).

John the Baptist testifies that he saw the Spirit descend from heaven like a dove and remain on Jesus, and that the One who sent him said that the one upon whom the Spirit descends and remains is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit. This shows that Jesus received the Spirit without measure ([ref:Joh 1:32-33|John 1:32-33]).
In Christ it was God's will that all fullness should dwell – this emphasizes that the Spirit and God's nature are given to the Son without limitation ([ref:Kol 1:19|Colossians 1:19]).
In Christ dwells all the fullness of deity in bodily form. This confirms that God gives the Spirit without measure to the Son ([ref:Kol 2:9|Colossians 2:9]).

God sent His Son into the world not to condemn the world, but so that the world might be saved through Him. The One whom God has sent with His word has a saving purpose – and this is the context for John 3:34 ([ref:Joh 3:17|John 3:17]).

Isaiah prophesies that the Lord's Spirit shall rest upon the shoot from Jesse's root – the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and strength, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the Lord. This points to the fact that the Messiah receives the Spirit in full measure ([ref:Jes 11:2|Isaiah 11:2]).

Jesus says in His high-priestly prayer that He has given the disciples the words He received from the Father, and they have accepted them. This confirms that Jesus' words are God's words, passed on from the Father ([ref:Joh 17:8|John 17:8]).
